articles.title: Custom jerseys, glam squads and TikTok: The college WAG has come a long way from tailgating
articles.summary: From professional gameday glam to custom jerseys and TikTok fame, college football girlfriends are redefining WAG culture while navigating criticism and find...
articles.body:
Hannah Cleveland 's dad was sitting in the stands at Beaver Stadium — home of Penn State's Nittany Lions — during their home game against Wisconsin a couple of weeks ago when he happened to glance at the phone of a woman sitting nearby. There was his daughter, getting her makeup done in a TikTok video .

"That's my daughter on your screen," he told the stranger.

Moments like that happen when you're a college football WAG — as in, the wife or girlfriend of a player — these days. Cleveland falls somewhere in the middle; she's the fiancée of Penn State wide receiver Chase Sowell .

The high school sweethearts spent much of their college years dating long distance, with Cleveland studying at Texas A&M while Sowell played college football out of state. Between classes, friends and her own commitments, she couldn't always make it to his games. Now that she's graduated and living with him during his final college season at Penn State, she has more time to embrace the gameday experience — including the occasional professional glam session.

The makeup artist behind Cleveland's gameday transformation, Allison Kaye , bills herself as the "inventor of Game Day Glam" on Instagram. She typically has NFL WAGs in her chair; this season alone, she's worked her way through the Dallas Cowboys, Buffalo Bills and Cincinnati Bengals contingents. But she's recently opened up her "glam suite" to the partners of college football players after noticing that they too were stepping up their sideline style and social media presence.

In an era where the biggest pop star on the planet spends her Sundays at Arrowhead and college coaches' wives are turning up at Paris Fashion Week , cheering on your jock sweetheart doesn't look like it used to.

Scroll through college football TikTok, and the WAG of it all is hard to miss.

Alongside the usual content of students getting ready to tailgate with the masses , you'll find women showing off custom outfits emblazoned with their partners' numbers, documenting pre- and postgame reunions , road-tripping to away games and meeting up with other girlfriends.

Some explicitly call themselves college WAGs. Others are simply participating in rituals that would look right at home on the feed of an NFL wife or girlfriend, who have become a social media genre unto themselves.

The fascination with college football girlfriends isn't exactly new. In 2013, Katherine Webb became a national talking point when television cameras lingered on her cheering for her then-boyfriend (now husband), Alabama quarterback A.J. McCarron. But where fans once just caught glimpses of players' girlfriends in the stands, they can now follow along with their lives before, during and after the game.

"It feels new because it is so intimate," Cara Hawkins-Jedlicka , a professor at Washington State University who studies sports and social media, tells Yahoo. "Fans are increasingly following athletes as people rather than performers. And WAG content gives backstage access," often through the everyday rituals of someone close to the player.

The result is a familiar part of college life being repackaged for an audience well beyond the stadium stands. Kaye noticed the evolution and wanted to be a part of it.

"Nobody needs glam for gameday," she tells Yahoo. "It's just all a part of the experience to go along with custom outfits and the girls all hanging out together."

Videos from Kaye's college glam suites at Ohio State and Penn State have drawn hundreds of thousands of views.

Sure, it's not the main event. But for a generation that's grown up documenting its life online, getting ready can be as much a part of the content as the game itself.

"Gen Z really has had to think of themselves as a personal brand for most of their lives," says Hawkins-Jedlicka.

That can make being a college football girlfriend a particularly appealing niche. A gameday GRWM offers a recognizable format, a built-in sports audience and a glimpse into a world that followers might not otherwise see. It's also a point of entry for these women to build their own audiences.

"'Get ready with me for college gameday as a WAG' is going to get your face in front of more viewers than 'Watch me prepare for my midterm exam and how I study,'" Hawkins-Jedlicka points out.

The girlfriends aren't new. It's the WAG culture that's changing.

For women who experienced WAG life before gameday GRWMs and professional glam suites became social media content, the difference is striking.

Tiffany Compton , who is married to former NFL player Tom Compton, recently reflected on how much gameday culture has changed since her husband's league debut in 2013. "I can't stress how different things used to be," she wrote in a TikTok featuring photos from his playing years, which ended in 2022. "The only thing I did prior to game days was make sure my beer bong was in the trunk for the tailgate."

She said it wasn't until 2019 that she even considered what she'd wear to games before Sunday rolled around. After seeing a video of college WAGs getting their makeup done, she concluded, "I fear we have lost the plot entirely."

Amari Hamilton , wife of Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Ty Hamilton, has experienced WAG life at both the college and NFL levels. Ty spent all five seasons of his college career at Ohio State, giving Amari and the other girlfriends years to form a tight-knit community around the same team.

In a recent TikTok , she remembered the college years as simpler. The girlfriends were young, hanging out and going through roughly the same stage of life together. In the NFL, she said, there are marriages, children, careers and families competing for that time.

But college football itself has changed too. Between NIL deals , the transfer portal and social media, players are becoming recognizable personalities long before they reach the pros. And as their profiles grow, so does the visibility of the people beside them.

Hawkins-Jedlicka says players' partners can contribute to that visibility, sometimes providing the kind of relatable, behind-the-scenes content that athletes themselves don't have the time or instincts to create.

"You're getting a secondhand look at what your favorite football player is doing through his girlfriend," she says.

In some cases, she notes, the women may be doing some of the branding work themselves — understanding social media trends, creating content and making their partners more accessible to fans. And while that can amount to unpaid labor, it may also provide opportunities for these women to develop their own audiences and brands.

Even so, some viewers seem to think that college-age women embracing the label "WAG" might be getting ahead of themselves.

"Oh lord help me, this is not the NFL," one viewer commented on Kaye's college glam content. "WAG is crazy, they're kids," wrote another. "This is so cute, but do college guys really have wives??" someone asked.

Others were ready for the young women supporting their athlete partners to have their moment. "Love that the college girls are getting their flowers cause it's not easy!" read one comment.

The reactions raise an interesting question about who gets to claim the WAG identity in the first place. Some sports fans seem uncomfortable with college-age women adopting the label.

Hawkins-Jedlicka understands some of that hesitation. Building an identity around a romantic partner can be risky at any age, she says, but particularly when you're still figuring out who you are.

"It's hard to look at 19-year-olds building their identity around someone else," she says. "I'd say that in general for men and women."

But she also sees another possibility: These women aren't necessarily defining their entire futures around their boyfriends. "A lot of them may be trying to find their own personal brand, their niche to play around with content and see what works," she says.

For the women actually living it, the label doesn't necessarily carry quite so much weight.

Cleveland wasn't even sure what to make of the "WAG" label at first. "I was like, 'What does the title even mean?'" she tells Yahoo. "But now I think it's kind of fun. I think you have to play into it a little bit."

Since Sowell joined Penn State , Cleveland has posted videos that show her putting together a fall camp basket for her fiancé and customizing accessories with his name and number. But she's still prioritizing her own pursuits.

Now working remotely and pursuing a master's degree, Cleveland is finding more time for the fun stuff too — traveling to games, tailgating with other players' partners and, yes, spending a Saturday morning getting glammed.

"It's a whole new ballpark, honestly," she says. "I like embracing it. I think it's fun."

Sharing her experiences online has also connected her with women whose partners play for other schools, but who understand the strange experience of having weekends dictated by a football schedule.

"It's a little bit lonely sometimes," says Cleveland.

Other WAGs, like Chloe Van Berkel , get it.

Her boyfriend, Charlie Sasso , is a senior playing football at Monmouth University, where Van Berkel quickly learned that gameday dressing is serious business. She's seen women spend $200 on custom outfits, with some shopping months before kickoff.

A postgrad herself, Van Berkel makes it to games when she can, though it isn't exactly the NFL WAG lifestyle: She's paying for it herself. One attempt to attend an away game in Nashville cost her and her friends around $700 each before their flight was canceled.

Her boyfriend isn't planning to pursue football professionally, either. That's part of why Van Berkel wants to make something of it now.

When she joked in a TikTok that becoming an NFL wife was "the dream," but "you gotta hold it down in college first," someone told her to "dream bigger." But she went to nursing school, works in social media and has plans of her own . Wearing her boyfriend's number on Saturday doesn't cancel any of that out.

"The whole dream doesn't have to be supporting my boyfriend," she says. "But if someone wants that, who cares?"

Maybe that's the appeal of the college WAG era happening online right now. Nobody needs to know whether a boyfriend is going pro, whether the relationship ends in marriage or whether today's custom jersey will mean anything in five years.

For now, these women are making something of the experience they're having — and bringing the internet along for the ride.

"The best way to enjoy things and enjoy life is to just romanticize it," says Van Berkel. "If you want to romanticize being a college athlete's girlfriend, why not?"

articles.title: "Virtually Catatonic": 49ers Legend Steve Young Needed an IV Drip After Vomiting From Drinking Following Historic Super Bowl Win
articles.summary: Who would have thought that a night of celebration win would turn into a medical emergency for Steve Young? On January 29, 1995, Steve Young finally got his...
articles.body:
Who would have thought that a night of celebration win would turn into a medical emergency for Steve Young?

On January 29, 1995, Steve Young finally got his chance to shine on football's biggest stage. Young put on a show in Super Bowl XXIX, throwing a record six touchdown passes, leading the San Francisco 49ers to a 49-26 win over the San Diego Chargers.

After the game ended, Young headed for the interviews, where he spent a long time. It was also uncomfortably hot that night. Veteran Peter King, in an appearance on 25 Whistles and who was working for Sports Illustrated at the time, recalled that Young had asked if he could get something to drink. King got him three Gatorades, which Young drank in minutes.

"By the time we got in the car to go back to his hotel, he pukes a red torrent of puke all over the back of this limo," King said. "When we got back to the hotel, he had like a junior suite … And he was so dehydrated, he was virtually catatonic. The Miami-Dade Fire Rescue came up into his room, and they didn't put one IV of saline in him; they put two IV in him."

Per Sports Illustrated, Young's agent at the time, Leigh Steinberg recalled Young lying on the bed with his arms outstretched, "like a death-bed scene," resembling "the last supper or something."

However, according to King, the quarterback was still entertaining those who came to talk with him, including former teammates from BYU. Young, even in that state, was still able to bask in the happiness of his performance.

"At one point, he just looks up and he goes, 'What an unbelievable day.' He said, 'I never threw six touchdown passes as a kid in Connecticut. I never threw six in high school. Never threw six in college. Never threw six obviously in the NFL. And I did it in the biggest game of my life. How incredible is that?'

"He was just, even though he was weak as a kitten at that time, he was just so happy. As happy as I've ever seen a human being after winning the Super Bowl."

Young had reason to be jubilant. Once an afterthought for the 49ers during the time Joe Montana led the charge, Young proved doubters wrong with this Super Bowl victory.

He put up solid numbers on the field too. Steve Young completed 24 of 36 passes for 325 yards and six touchdowns without throwing an interception. He and the 49ers continued their legacy of being a Super Bowl contender even in Montana's absence. The Super Bowl XXIX was the only one that Young won as a starter; the other two he had won at San Francisco were as a backup to Montana.

However, even with two IV lines pumping saline into him, Young had a clear mind. Someone in the room said, "Joe, who?" to which Young took offense.

"No, don't do that!" he replied. "Joe's a good guy."

Per SI, King was with Steve until 3 am, and he later wrote up his assignment.

"It was less a file and more like a complete story—he estimates 1,500 to 2,000 words long; [Michael] Silver guesses more like 3,000—with a scene opener, dialogue and a ton of details, topped by the symbolic moment of an exhausted Super Bowl MVP purging himself. It was, King knew, journalistic gold," Chris Ballard wrote for Sports Illustrated.

articles.title: Drake Maye’s biggest supporter is Ann Michael, and her journey from UNC graduate to Patriots fan favorite is worth knowing
articles.summary: Ann Michael Maye has spent more than a decade beside Drake Maye, and New England now knows her almost as well as it knows him.
articles.body: Ann Michael Maye has spent more than a decade beside Drake Maye, and New England now knows her almost as well as it knows him. The Patriots quarterback met her in middle school, followed her to the same college and married her in June 2025. She earned her UNC business degree that May and then moved to Boston to build a life around his NFL career. Fans noticed quickly. Between her viral baking videos and a hoodie she wore to a playoff game, she has become one of the team's most recognised faces off the field.Who is Ann Michael Maye, Drake Maye's biggest supporter?Ann Michael Hudson was born on August 11, 2003, in Huntersville, North Carolina, and grew up around football. Her father played at Wofford College. Her younger brother, Tad, was one of Drake's backup quarterbacks at UNC in 2023 before he moved to Coastal Carolina.She and Drake started dating at 12. Both went to William A. Hough High School in Cornelius, and they made the relationship Instagram-official in January 2020. After graduation, both chose Chapel Hill.Her own résumé is strong. She earned a business degree from UNC's Kenan-Flagler Business School in 2025, with minors in entrepreneurship and conflict management. She served as vice president of finance in her sorority and held an internship at Deloitte Consulting. She finished at 21, a year behind Drake in age but right alongside him in ambition. She was also with Drake on draft night in 2024, when New England took him third overall, and after college she left North Carolina, the only home she had known, to live near him in Boston.Drake proposed in January 2025, soon after his rookie season ended. The wedding followed on June 21 at Grandfather Golf and Country Club in Linville.How did Ann Michael Maye become a Patriots fan favorite?It started with food. Her Bakemas videos went viral, and by January she said she had finished filming a baking show of her own. Her TikTok comments fill up with Patriots fans, and some now call her the first lady of New England. A football household likely helped too. Growing up with a father and brother who played the game, she already knew how a long season feels.She also shows up. Before the Divisional Round game against the Texans, she arrived at Gillette Stadium in an "I Heart Drake Maye" sweatshirt, the same design many fans had been wearing. She has also joined Dave Portnoy for a pizza review in Needham.Calling her the biggest supporter is fair, but she does not hold that role alone. After the Wild Card win over the Chargers, Drake talked about his parents and brothers first, then added, "And obviously, Ann Michael, so I can't forget about her." His parents, Mark and Aimee, are at every game too.What sets her apart is the timing. articles.title: Travis Kelce's 1.7 billion franchise gets major boost after Guardians' dramatic ALDS comeback
articles.summary: Travis Kelce had plenty to celebrate as the Cleveland Guardians completed a remarkable comeback in the American League Division Series.
articles.body: Travis Kelce had plenty to celebrate as the Cleveland Guardians completed a remarkable comeback in the American League Division Series. The Kansas City Chiefs star watched from the stands as Cleveland defeated the Chicago White Sox 2-0 in Game 5 on October 10, sealing a series victory after losing the opening two games. Now a minority owner of the Guardians, Kelce shared his excitement after witnessing the team fight its way into the American League Championship Series. His message was clear: he believes Cleveland has plenty left to accomplish this postseason.Travis Kelce backs the Guardians after their ALDS triumphCleveland's comeback gave Kelce another reason to show his support for his hometown team. After the Guardians fell behind in the series, they won three consecutive games to eliminate Chicago and keep their championship hopes alive.Speaking after the decisive victory, Kelce made his confidence in the team clear."The ALCS is ours baby, I can feel it," he said.He also spoke about the atmosphere surrounding the franchise and the excitement building among Cleveland fans."The energy in Cleveland is electric right now," he said. "Shout out to everybody. Go Guards, baby, Go Guards!"Kelce's enthusiasm reflects his growing connection to the Guardians beyond his role as a fan. The NFL tight end became a minority owner of the franchise earlier this season, adding another chapter to his long-standing relationship with Cleveland.The city has remained an important part of his identity despite his success with the Chiefs. Kelce has repeatedly credited his hometown for helping shape his life and career."I say it all the time: I’m a kid from the Heights living the dream," he said. "I credit every good thing in my life to Cleveland.”Guardians prepare for ALCS after José Ramírez and Gavin Williams deliverThe Guardians backed up Kelce's confidence with a strong finish to the ALDS. José Ramírez played a key role in the turnaround, recording two home runs and seven RBIs across the series. His two-run homer off Sean Burke proved decisive in Game 5, helping Cleveland secure the 2-0 victory.Kelce described the experience as a special moment in his life.“It was [more than a moment money could buy],” Kelce said in an article done by MLB.com, “one of the coolest moments of my life.”Cleveland's pitching staff also helped turn the series around. The team allowed just 10 runs across the final three games, while its 21-strikeout performance in Game 5 set a postseason record for a nine-inning game. The Guardians also recorded 19 strikeouts in Game 3, giving them the two highest totals in that category for a nine-inning postseason contest.Kelce also praised the bond among the players, highlighting the unity that helped Cleveland recover from its early setbacks.“This team has camaraderie,” Kelce continued Saturday night. “You can see how much energy they have for each other, how much love they have for each other. And that’s hard to beat..."The Guardians now turn their attention to the ALCS against the Tampa Bay Rays, with Game 1 scheduled for October 12. Cleveland will look to carry its momentum into the next round as it pursues a place in the World Series.For Kelce, the excitement is about more than a single win. articles.title: Winners and losers as Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Texans: 'I was praying something happened'
articles.summary: "I don't even know if I'm allowed to say [but] I was praying something happened with him," Garrett Wilson told Yahoo Sports after the Jets beat the Browns. "...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — In the New York Jets' postgame locker room on Sunday afternoon, Garrett Wilson lit up.

The former Ohio State receiver who became a top-10 pick in the NFL Draft was hearing the latest news of another former Ohio State receiver who became a top-10 pick in the draft.

And Wilson, who overlapped with Harrison for one season in Columbus, was thrilled to hear the Arizona Cardinals were trading Harrison to the Houston Texans .

"I don't even know if I'm allowed to say [but] I was praying something happened with him," Wilson told Yahoo Sports after the Jets beat the Browns . "The fact he did, and it's a spot like Houston? Man, I'm happy for him."

Who else is happy for the highly-touted prospect that didn't take off in two-plus Arizona seasons? And who might be disappointed that the Cardinals are dealing Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for 2027 second- and sixth-round picks?

Based on conversations with players and execs around the league, here are Yahoo Sports' winners and losers of the trade:

Cardinals' arsenal to rebuild: It was hardly a secret across the league that the Cardinals wanted a second-round draft pick and change in exchange for their physically gifted wideout. But multiple teams I spoke with in recent weeks were not convinced Harrison warranted that cost. One NFC talent evaluator told me last week they thought there was "zero chance" Harrison was worth a second- or third-round pick. A high-ranking AFC executive told me that for a Day 3 pick — that is, fourth round or later — the value would be worth pursuing Harrison, but no higher.

The Cardinals capitalized on a desperate Texans team that had reason to believe in Harrison more than 31 counterparts. And thus two seasons and four games after selecting Harrison fourth overall, the Cardinals not only get a second-round pick but they get a second-round pick in the talent-rich 2027 draft even amid trends to trade high 2028 picks (hi, Baltimore Ravens for Cam Jurgens and New England Patriots for A.J. Brown) to save up for the expected treasure trove in April.

C.J. Stroud: With Stroud at Ohio State in 2022, Harrison posted a whopping 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns in 13 games. The duo connected on three touchdowns in the Rose Bowl alone that season. Teammates from their time speak to the on-field chemistry quarterback and receiver built quickly, the work ethic that had them in the building early and the cerebral nature that helped them connect.

Stroud has played better this season than his team's 1-4 record suggests, completing 64.3% of his passes for 1,402 yards, six touchdowns and no interceptions in five games. He's rushed for another 71 yards and a score. But the Texans' receiving corps has proven incredibly shallow. Tank Dell has yet to return from injured reserve after knee surgery following a December dislocation of his kneecap and multiple torn ligaments. Jayden Higgins suffered a season-ending ACL tear during training camp. Nico Collins missed Weeks 2 and 3 with a hamstring strain suffered in practice. What can Harrison add? "They don't really miss now together," Wilson said. "C.J. don't miss much anyway, but when he got a guy like that, that got a catch radius like that, runs good routes? It's going to be fun to watch."

Marvin Harrison Jr.'s career: This trade is likely only a reality because of how much Harrison struggled in Arizona. A combination of 2025 health setbacks (concussion, appendicitis, two heel injuries) and target plummet this year meant he finishes his Cardinals tenure with 108 catches for 1,578 yards and 13 touchdowns in 33 games (30 starts). This season, Harrison had just 13 targets across four games; he caught five for 85 yards and a score. The high-ranking AFC executive believed Houston could ignite something in Harrison for reasons beyond the college reunion: the benefit of the excitement tends to follow a new trade acquisition, as opposed to the disappointment surrounding a high-draft pick that doesn't quickly materialize. Another AFC executive believed that even Harrison's up-and-down tenure in Arizona showed his speed, quickness and agility at the pro level. Turn those flashes into marks of consistency, and Texans fans have reason to be excited.

"I know the belief system that he's going to have around him in the Texans," Wilson said. "I know what he can do. So for me, it's just a ticking-time bomb with him. I can't wait to watch him erupt. He's got all the ability in the world and now he's playing with someone that he's been with before. They got great chemistry. And I saw it from Day 1 at O State. I can't wait to watch. You got me excited."

The chance the Texans defy history again: Since 1979, only seven times in NFL history has a team started 0-3 and advanced to the playoffs, per NBC Sports . The Texans claim two of those seven, most recently rebounding last year from 0-3 to 12-5. The Texans proved they belonged in the playoffs when they beat the Steelers in Pittsburgh, 30-6, in the wild-card round. The Patriots then outlasted the Texans 28-16 in the divisional round. Could the Texans rebound from 0-4 to make the playoffs? Only one team, the 1992 Chargers, have accomplished that feat. With 17 chances instead of 16, the Texans, now 1-4, have one more chance to showcase their upgraded roster than that Chargers team. Will it be enough?

The cost of desperation: The Texans needed to do something . Head coach DeMeco Ryans already stripped defensive coordinator Matt Burke of play-calling this past week . Pair that with an 0-4 start and a need to make a contract decision on Stroud soon, and Houston let Arizona squeeze more out of the deal than less-frenzied franchises would have copped. If the Texans advance deep into the playoffs, perhaps this pays off. But it's worth remembering that the Texans' defense has still regressed meaningfully from last year. Holding the winless Titans to three points in Sunday's victory is better than a loss, but the Titans have been held to 10 or fewer points in three of five games this year so it's not sufficient to prove the group is settling. What will it take for Harrison, whose fifth-year option decision looms in May, to justify the sacrifice of a more cost-controlled 2027 second-round pick in a talent-rich draft? If Harrison approaches his draft billing, it will be worth it. But two-plus seasons and several injuries in, as he scrambles to pick up a new offense midseason, how likely is that?

The 'film means everything' crowd: It's disingenuous to criticize Harrison's college career and the film that propelled him to the fourth overall pick. Harrison's 2,613 yards and 31 touchdowns, including two seasons in which he surpassed 1,200 yards and 14 touchdowns. He showed he could thrive with Stroud, and he showed he could thrive with quarterback Kyle McCord. So the Cardinals were comfortable spending big on him despite Harrison's decision to not participate in scouting combine drills. Two-and-a-half years later, some talent evaluators wonder how significant that decision was. While an AFC executive argued for the importance of production on the field rather than in the vacuum of test-like combine settings, talent evaluators from two NFC teams wondered if Harrison was "overdrafted" relative to his career thus far in part because of missing information about his physical traits compared to historical precedent.

"The perception was that he was fast and strong and explosive and all that, but now you question whether the testing [would have] come back a little bit underwhelming," one NFC evaluator told Yahoo Sports, "and then if it would have come back underwhelming, he wouldn't have been [drafted] as high."

NFC teams outside the NFC West: The NFC West sent three teams to the playoffs last season: the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers. All three won at least one playoff game, the NFC championship staged between the Rams and Seahawks before Seattle beat the Patriots for the Lombardi Trophy. The Rams entered this season with overwhelming Super Bowl odds, and the Niners and Seahawks started hotter than their Los Angeles foe through four weeks. The Cardinals were already going to be the weak link in the division, but with Harrison, the chance of the any-given-Sunday in-division upset drops further. And the chance of the NFC West's other three teams taking home two wins a pop vs. the Cardinals, helping them win not only a division berth but one to two wild-card berths, increases.

Cardinals' current offensive players: Few expected Arizona to win many games this season amid a rebuild, a hole in the quarterback room and what seemed to be an unforgiving schedule this year. With the Cardinals falling to 1-4 after this Sunday, that expectation might not change. But the offense's chance to function in head coach Mike LaFleur's first season does dip with the loss of Harrison. Even as Harrison commanded a lesser target share this season, the defensive attention he directed away from teammates was valuable. Harrison was on the field on 74% of offensive snaps through the Cardinals' first four games. That helped players like Michael Wilson and Trey McBride find creases in defenses, and it helped teammates like Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier face less-stacked boxes. articles.title: Cam Skattebo breathed a 'sigh of relief' after Commanders disaster overshadowed his fumble that squandered a chance for Giants win
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo kind of got bailed out by Commanders miscues. At least, for Skattebo, the bulk of the attention got shifted to Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn.
articles.body:
Before there was Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn frittering away an almost certain win there was Cam Skattebo.

The New York Giants were at Washington's 24-yard line Sunday with the game tied at 27 in need of only a field goal to secure a walkoff win in overtime. Rather than settle for a 41-yard kick, they ran the ball with Skattebo on first-and-10 in hope of getting into the end zone or, more likely, setting up Dominic Zvada for a shorter kick.

Neither happened. Instead, Skattebo fumbled, and the Commanders recovered. And what just seconds earlier looked like a Giants win turned into disaster for New York.

The Commanders instead had the ball with 1:55 remaining and a chance to drive for their own game-winning field-goal attempt.

They got into position to do so, and then they did this.

That's Daniels inexplicably running and getting tackled inbounds in field-goal range in the game's final seconds with no timeout.

And that's Quinn slamming his headset in frustration as the clock ticked down to zero on a 27-27 tie, his team having just squandered a chance at a win.

As for Skattebo, he was left off the hook by the play. Kind of.

Skattebo still fumbled away a likely Giants win. But instead of a loss, the Giants were gifted a tie. And the focus was taken off his late-game snafu and placed squarely on Daniels and Quinn instead.

For Skattebo, the moment added up to a "sigh of relief." But he recognized that he's not completely off the hook.

"It was a sigh of relief, you know," Skattebo told reporters at his locker. "I probably won't get reamed as much, but I'm still gonna get reamed. At the end of the day, my number was called, and I gave the ball up.

"If that happens again this year, I promise you that won't happen."

That's obviously not a promise Skattebo can guarantee to keep.

As for Sunday, Skattebo is content to not be the focus of the storyline on a Giants loss.

articles.title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs surpasses Barry Sanders for most NFL touchdowns scored before age 25
articles.summary: Gibbs could put that record far out of reach, not turning 25 until next March with 12 games remaining this season.
articles.body:
With two touchdowns in the Detroit Lions' 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, Jahmyr Gibbs surpassed Hall of Famer Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns scored before age 25 in his NFL career.

Gibbs had 56 TDs coming into Sunday's game, one behind Sanders on that particular list . He doesn't turn 25 until next March and the Lions had 13 games remaining on their 2026-27 schedule. So the fourth-year star had plenty of time to overtake the Lions legend.

The first of Gibbs' scores came on a 1-yard run early in the second quarter. That finished off a seven-play, 54-yard drive that tied the score at 7 after Detroit punted on its previous four possessions.

Gibbs overtook Sanders for the top spot in the fourth quarter. The Lions were already ahead 38-14 when he rushed on a play designed to go left. Faced with a wall of Arizona defenders, Gibbs changed direction — the type of play that invites some comparisons to Sanders — and dashed to the right, outrunning everyone to the right corner of the end zone.

The box score says Gibbs' TD was a 3-yard run, but he covered far more ground than that. It was another example of how much difficulty the Cardinals had trying to corral the Lions' star running back throughout the game.

In addition to his two TDs, Gibbs finished with 151 yards rushing on 25 carries. He added 56 yards receiving on five catches, compiling over 200 yards from scrimmage against an Arizona defense that ranked 23rd in the NFL with 1,405 yards allowed (and 20th with 470 rushing yards).

Five games into an already impressive career, Gibbs has recorded 46 rushing touchdowns and 12 receiving scores. He has 4,044 rushing yards and 581 yards receiving, emerging as the dual threat out of the backfield that the Lions envisioned when they selected him No. 12 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft.

Following Sunday's performance, Gibbs ranks second in the NFL with 504 rushing yards and is tied for the league lead with seven touchdowns.

Draft observers and Lions fans may remember that Gibbs' selection wasn't viewed favorably at the time. The perception across the NFL and those who cover it was that running backs were no longer impact players worth a high draft pick. Additionally, Detroit had signed free-agent running back David Montgomery, presumably to be the featured player at that position.

Four years later, no one is questioning the Lions for drafting Gibbs with a top-15 selection, nor for making him the highest-paid running back in the league with a three-year, $67.5 million contract extension during training camp this year.

One question that remains through the remainder of the 2026-27 season is how much distance Gibbs will put between him and Sanders — and other NFL greats including Randy Moss, Emmitt Smith and Jim Brown. If he follows his career averages of 14 rushing TDs and four receiving scores per season, Gibbs may put that record far out of reach.

articles.title: 5 momentous plays in Week 5: Another Sirianni mistake, plus Giants and Commanders both blowing a win
articles.summary: The Eagles blew the game prior to the final kickoff, and somehow both the Giants and Commanders blew overtime.
articles.body:
Bad news, Eagles fans: Your coach is back in the "momentous plays" list, and not in a good way.

For a second straight week, Nick Sirianni and the Eagles found themselves on the wrong end of a game they absolutely should have won.

In Week 4, it was coughing up a 10-point lead at home to the Rams. On Sunday, it was kicking off with a lead and eight seconds remaining … and somehow losing to the Jaguars in London.

Keeping it in the NFC East, we also had a game where both teams arguably coughed up a "sure" win in overtime . It's perhaps only fitting that there were zero NFC East victories in Week 5, even with two division teams going head to head.

We also scoured well beyond the NFC East to find Week 5's most momentous plays that shifted the tide in games dramatically.

1. The Eagles actually lost prior to kicking off inbounds

Yes, you absolutely can question why Nick Sirianni kicked inbounds to a team with no timeouts after taking the lead with just eight seconds left . It's fair criticism, and it cost the Eagles the game in the end.

But the way they mismanaged the clock prior to that point can't be dismissed. They had a chance to end it before the ensuing kickoff.

On second-and-10 from the Jacksonville 34-yard line with 21 seconds remaining and the Jaguars leading, 16-14, the Eagles threw a quick out to rookie Makai Lemon. It was a good play-call, netting 7 yards and improving the field position for the go-ahead field goal Jake Elliott would eventually make.

But there was too much time on the clock, and Lemon ran out of bounds after his catch, stopping the clock with 17 seconds left. Had Lemon just caught the ball and fallen down inbounds, the Jaguars would have been forced to call their final timeout around that same time, or perhaps a second or two fewer.

On third down, the Eagles could have run the ball and called timeout with just a few seconds left. That would have made Elliott's kick the final play of the game, win or lose. Then there's no kickoff to worry about.

The worst part is that the Jaguars called timeout before first down after the Eagles hit a big play to enter field-goal territory. (And they even did a favor to Philly, letting 20 seconds tick off the clock before burning it.) That should have been ample time for Siranni to instruct his players how to handle a catch and that they should not go out of bounds.

Instead, with the clock stopped after Lemon's catch, the Jaguars used their final timeout after Dameon Pierce's third-down carry. There were only eight seconds left when Elliott kicked off to the Jaguars, but those took a virtual eternity to tick off while Ameer Abdullah was running back the kickoff that set up Cam Little's miracle game-winner.

Every call Jaguars head coach Liam Coen made Sunday seemed to backfire, and yet one simple play — well, two really — came back to bite Sirianni. That's two straight weeks now where the Eagles were in a dominant position to win each game and ended up losing both.

2. Commanders blew OT, but so did the Giants

The Commanders botched the end of overtime about as badly as possible. They had the ball, ample time and downs to win the game and Jayden Daniels seemed to have no clue what was going on .

Blame Daniels, blame Dan Quinn — both are fair game.

This was also the rare game where you reasonably could experience equal rancor for how both teams handled their chances to win. The Giants also should have won, despite the Commanders being up 14 with eight minutes left.

Never mind Washington's self-inflicted mistakes, missing an extra point and committing some critical penalties, including one that wiped out a Jameis Winston interception. The Giants had the ball and needed only to set up a game-winning kick attempt.

They were in business with first-and-10 at the Washington 24-yard line in overtime, under the two-minute stoppage and with the Commanders out of timeouts. All they needed to do was run it three times, center the ball where Dominic Zvada wanted it and go home a winner. An ugly winner, no doubt, but better than a loss or tie.

Instead, Cam Skattebo fumbled it — the one thing he couldn't do. The Commanders recovered, moved the ball 53 yards in six plays and should have won, had it not been for Daniels' clock-killing exploits .

When the clock ran out with the game still tied, Skattebo breathed a sigh of relief . He was lucky his fumble didn't end in a Giants loss. It should have been a win.

3. 49ers rookie provides massive play in huge win

The 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seahawks featured 12 scoring drives, but it really was a defensive grinder for most of it. There was no bigger play in that regard than right before halftime.

The 49ers took an early edge, but the Seahawks started shifting things back in their favor, perhaps inspired by the ejection of the 49ers' Dre Greenlaw . After cutting the 49ers' lead to 14-13, the Seahawks forced a punt, which was downed at the Seattle 1-yard line.

That backed the Seahawks up in the final 20 seconds of the half, and they couldn't simply bleed out the clock because the 49ers had all three timeouts left. On the first play, disaster struck for the home team: 49ers defensive tackle Gracen Halton stripped Seahawks running back George Holani in the end zone and recovered the fumble for a touchdown.

That made it 21-13, San Francisco, at the half. The Seahawks were getting the ball back to start the third quarter, but instead of being able to take the lead, the best they could have done was tie the game.

Granted, there were three second-half lead changes after that point. But the 49ers needed every score they could get on the road, and that one possession was a massive swing at a critical time when the winds had been shifting Seattle's direction.

The rookie Halton had a massive game, also adding a sack, two big run stuffs and a pressure on Sam Darnold's fourth-down pass to Cooper Kupp that came up inches short of a first down, handing the game over to the 49ers.

4. Browns miss multiple chances to beat Jets

The Cleveland Browns had been one of the league's better stories, hitting a 3-1 mark through the first month of the season, but they gave away Sunday's game at the Jets . Even though momentum had shifted in the Browns' favor in the fourth quarter, they could never take advantage of the chances they had.

It all started in the fourth quarter. On the first play of the fourth, Browns rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren intercepted Geno Smith on third down, but Maliek Collins jumped offsides, negating the interception and moving the Jets into field-goal range. Jason Sanders made the 54-yarder to push Cleveland's deficit to 10-6.

Just over 30 game seconds later, the Browns were back in business in Jets territory after Isaiah Bond's 30-yard catch. What followed: illegal formation penalty, sack, delay of game, then another sack. It moved the ball from the New York 45-yard line to the Cleveland 27. The Browns punted on fourth-and-38.

The Jets did the Browns a favor by punting on fourth-and-1 with 10-plus minutes left, and Cleveland moved down the field for the go-ahead score after trailing most of the game. The missed extra point didn't help, but it wasn't the Browns' most fateful mistake.

Smith's lost fumble at his own 43-yard line with 4:20 left was a huge gift, but the Browns couldn't do anything with the ball, using only 19 seconds of clock. On fourth-and-10, the Jets punted — or attempted to. The rain-soaked snap sailed over Corey Bojorquez's head, and the Jets scored a TD three plays later to take the lead.

The Browns had two possessions in the final 3:01 of the game but could do nothing with either. That fateful sequence with the missed PAT and botched snap helped turn a potential Browns edge into a Jets win in the rain.

5. Chargers' biggest blow came before Herbert's late turnovers

The Chargers fell to 0-5, but they had real designs on their first victory of the season. Once again, Justin Herbert's fourth-quarter turnovers — his fifth and sixth of the season — were at the center of the narrative.

But the roots of the Chargers' 23-17 loss to the Broncos can also be traced back one possession earlier.

The Chargers took their first lead late in the third quarter on Kimani Vidal's 42-yard TD run, which came immediately after Tuli Tuipulotu had forced and recovered a Bo Nix fumble. The Broncos had looked stagnant offensively most of the game, even with Sean Payton taking back play-calling duties.

The teams traded punts, as the Chargers' defense stood tall all game, and when Wil Lutz missed a 42-yard field-goal try, it felt like it might be L.A.'s day. But Herbert and the offense couldn't do enough to help pull off the win.

The Chargers lost their little ripple of offensive mojo and stalled at the worst time. Herbert scrambled on third-and-9, and he was marked just short of the line to gain at their own 41-yard line — about the length of the football. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel called for a QB sneak, and Herbert has been very effective on those in his career, but he was stood up immediately and stopped short.

That started the avalanche that followed: a Broncos touchdown and two Herbert turnovers, both of which led to field goals. You can't blame LA's defense for that. The Chargers' offensive miscues flipped a 17-10 Chargers lead into 13 unanswered points and a 23-17 loss .

Herbert's failed sneak opened the door for the Broncos to pull off the comeback. Had the Chargers converted and drained more clock — while resting an exhausted defense a bit more — and perhaps even put up some points, it would have been a different ending. Cameron Dicker still has big range, and the Chargers needed about 20 yards to have given him a shot.

Instead, they turned it over on downs, which was as big and perhaps bigger than the later mistakes.

articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered a rib injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit in the pocket.

ESPN's Adam Schefter noted Penix will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury:

Henry, Huntley Win the Game for Ravens 🐦‍⬛

After missing the Falcons' drive in overtime, Penix told reporters following the game that he doesn't believe it will be a long-term injury, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi :

Head coach Kevin Stefanski had previously provided more information on the injured quarterback after the contest.

"I hope he's great," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson about Penix, per Raimondi . "I hope that it could maybe only be just a bruise or something like that, and it just felt a little like that in the moment, but I just pray he's all right. I know the whole team does."

Penix, 26, had a solid game, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. But on the final drive in regulation he took a big hit from Tavius Robinson and fumbled, though Atlanta managed to recover the loose ball.

The game then went into overtime and the Ravens scored a touchdown on their first possession. Penix remained on the bench and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, who threw a pick on the second play of the drive.

Injuries have been a massive story in Penix's career. The young quarterback only appeared in nine games last season after suffering a left ACL injury that required season-ending surgery. He missed the first two games of the NFL season but provided a spark upon his return, as Atlanta had won two games in a row heading into Sunday night.

Penix also tore his ACL twice in college, and shoulder injuries also cost him significant time at the college level. It's been a bumpy road from a health perspective.

Depending on the severity of this latest injury, Tagovailoa could be called back into action. He was released by the Miami Dolphins ahead of the 2026 campaign after a string of disappointing seasons, though he brings plenty of experience (76 career starts) to the position.

articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have a once-in-a-generation talent in NFL All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton — a player they can ill afford to lose after he was hurt against the Atlanta Falcons in Sunday's Week 5 game.

"Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton is running off to the sideline after being looked at by trainers," ESPN's Jamison Hensley wrote on his official X account. "He's headed to the sideline medical tent."

Hamilton's time off the field was brief — he returned to the game on a 4th & 2 for the Falcons, with the Ravens trailing 17-15 in the 3rd quarter.

"Kyle Hamilton trying to get back in the game on 4th-and-2," The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec wrote on his official X account. "He did."

Ravens Broke Bank for Kyle Hamilton in 2025

Hamilton and the Ravens agreed to a massive, $100.4 million contract extension in August 2025 that made him the highest-paid safety in NFL history and keeps the 2-time NFL All-Pro with the team through 2029.

The deal also includes another record-setting number: $82 million in guaranteed money.

"All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton and the Baltimore Ravens reached agreement today on a four-year, $100.4 million extension, the largest for a safety in NFL history," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on August 27. "The deal … includes $82 million guaranteed — which surpasses the previous record of $45M for a Safety."

Hamilton, who is only 25 years old, was in the final season of the 4-year, $16.25 million contract he signed with the Ravens after they selected him in the first round (No. 14 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft.

Relief After Kyle Hamilton Returns to Game

If there is one defender the Ravens couldn't stand to lose, it's Hamilton.

"Hamilton's versatility has been essential for the Ravens," Barnwell wrote. With the defense struggling to start the season, coordinator Zach Orr moved Hamilton back into the box, where he has had a James-like impact around the line of scrimmage. articles.title: Heat rookie cites a specific aspect that he’s looking to take from Klay Thompson
articles.summary: MIAMI – As the Miami Heat will be led by the dynamic duo of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, there will also be young players who will look to make an...
articles.body:
MIAMI – As the Miami Heat will be led by the dynamic duo of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo, there will also be young players who will look to make an immediate impact, such as rookie Ryan Conwell. While the Heat rookie has already been shouted out by the likes of Klay Thompson , the second-round pick would reveal what he has taken away from the four-time champion with the Golden State Warriors.

In Miami's 125-124 preseason loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves, Conwell would get an extended role with the team as the projected starters of Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Thompson, Andrew Wiggins, and Davion Mitchell didn't play. Along with some of the rotational players being absent, Conwell showed many traits, including his three-point ability that was present in college.

Heat's Ryan Conwell on what he's seen Klay Thompson do all the time

Selected with the 37th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, the Heat took Conwell, who recorded a year each with a different school such as USF, Indiana State, Xavier, and Louisville. The three-point ability was really showcased starting with Indiana State, as he shot over 40 percent from deep with the Sycamores and Xavier, and while it dipped to 34.5 percent with the Cardinals, he attempted 9.6 three-point shots per game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

In Saturday's preseason contest, Conwell would log a game-high 22 points on seven of 18 shooting from the field, two of nine from deep, six of seven from the free-throw line, to go along with nine assists, five rebounds, and two steals.

On Saturday, Miami's coaching staff ran a ton of plays with Conwell shooting motion threes off an inbound pass, which the team wants him to do more of, as it helps; he's seen Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr. do it many times.

"Yeah, they definitely are," Conwell said when asked if the team is pushing him to take those types of shots. "They pour a lot of confidence into me every day, and I get a lot of confidence from the work I put in in the gym with the other coaches as well. Also, I mean, I watch Klay and Tim do it all the time, so I'm just learning every day, and yeah, just putting in the work."

Despite the two-of-nine clip from deep, there's no denying that the team and Conwell aren't worried about his sharpshooter mentality.

Heat's Erik Spoelstra on Ryan Conwell overcoming the "ups and downs"

Conwell's three-point ability has been hyped ever since he was taken by the Heat in the 2026 NBA Draft, with Thompson himself saying during training camp that the rookie beat him in a shooting drill. However, Saturday's outing showcased Conwell's playmaking ability, as the 22-year-old has been tasked with learning to initiate the offense for Miami, especially since the point-guard depth has been hit with Dru Smith's calf injury.

While the nine assists are encouraging, head coach Erik Spoelstra would tell ClutchPoints that he's overcoming the "ups and downs" he's had in training camp, further explaining the trust he had in the guard during the preseason loss.

"Well, he showed the fortitude to stick with it. He's had some ups and downs in training camp, welcome to the league as a young player, but we feel he has the makeup to be able to weather all these things that will continue to happen when you're a young player. You can see what he's made of," Spoelstra said.

"He made some big plays in the second half as he got settled into the game; you can feel his competitive spirit on both ends of the court, and made some really nice plays," Spoelstra continued. "Obviously, had a couple threes that were big, but he made some plays off the dribble, and we were running, you know, some of the triggers in the fourth quarter, really, for him to make the read, whether it was a shot or get us into something, and he did a nice job with it."

Heat's Ryan Conwell on the game slowing down for him

While Conwell wouldn't connect on what could've been the game-winning shot with time expiring in the fourth quarter, the performance overall shouldn't be undervalued. His words shouldn't be undersold as well, as he told ClutchPoints after the game that aside from gaining more comfortability with the team, "the game is slowing down each day."

"First and foremost, want to give all glory to God. I'm just blessed to be in this position, part of a great organization," Conwell said. "But credit to my coaching staff and to my vets. You know, every day in practice, I'm able just to work on my reads, work on different things, different pieces of my game, and I think with each day, it's showing out there on the floor. It's getting more and more comfortable. The game is slowing down each day, so it's just a work in progress, and I'm just trying to get better at it every single day, just to be an all-around player."

At any rate, it remains to be seen how Conwell's role will be with Miami come the regular-season opener on Oct. 21 against the Minnesota Timberwolves, but he'll continue fine-tuning his skills in the upcoming preseason contest on Wednesday against the Brooklyn Nets.

articles.title: NFL: San Francisco 49ers & Minnesota Vikings go 5-0
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings maintain their perfect starts to the season on another gripping Sunday in the NFL.
articles.body:
Week five in the NFL was a wild one from the very first play in London to overtime in Atlanta 14 hours later.

Sunday started with a disallowed touchdown and two players being ejected on the first play at Tottenham, before two field goals in the final eight seconds helped the Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Philadelphia Eagles.

That was a sign of things to come as frantic finishes became a theme, including a farcial overtime climax in Washington as the Commanders tied with the New York Giants.

Big wins for the Green Bay Packers, New England Patriots and Detroit Lions moved that trio to 3-2 for the season, while the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings became the first teams to go 5-0.

Here's the pick of Sunday's week five action.

San Francisco beat Super Bowl champions Seattle 32-29 in a typically brutal contest between divisional rivals, with the Niners having defensive star Dre Greenlaw ejected early on for a headbutt on Ernest Jones, who was not wearing a helmet, on the sidelines.

Both defences are elite and forced a season-high seven turnovers in the game, with the 49ers in particular taking advantage by scoring three touchdowns from theirs. The 21 points off turnovers was the most Seattle have allowed in a decade.

Brock Purdy eventually got San Francisco over the line thanks to new wide receiver Mike Evans, who had 113 yards receiving and a touchdown, taking some great catches late on.

The only team to have a top-five scoring offence and defence, the 49ers again have injury problems this season, but if Evans stays fit he could be the missing piece in the puzzle.

San Francisco are now 5-0 for the third time under head coach Kyle Shanahan. They made the Super Bowl on both previous occasions and, if they keep finding ways to win, they have every chance again.

The Minnesota Vikings are also 5-0 after another defensive masterclass from Brian Flores' unit in their 23-13 win at the slumping New Orleans Saints.

With wins over the Saints (1-4), Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) and Miami Dolphins (0-5), we will know more about the Vikings after their bye, but allowing only 13 points a game will always give you a chance.

Commanders and Giants star in comedy of errors

There was a comedy of errors at the end of the Washington Commanders' 27-27 tie with the New York Giants as both teams fluffed their lines with victory within their grasp.

The Giants scored two late touchdowns to force overtime but, when within range of a winning field goal, they ran the ball with Cam Skattebo, who fumbled to lose possession.

Washington then had the game at their mercy in the dying seconds but, instead of taking the kick, ran a play - and ran out of time.

With play-calling like that, neither team deserved to win.

The Baltimore Ravens showed them both how it is done as quarterback Lamar Jackson's back-up Tyler Huntley earned a 30-23 overtime victory at the Atlanta Falcons, throwing a touchdown with 40 seconds left of regulation time before running in the game-winner in the extra period.

More poor finishing came in the rain in New York as the Cleveland Browns missed an extra point and then Corey Bojorquez fumbled a late punt which the Jets turned into the winning touchdown.

Although it was messy at times, the Jets seem to have a fine defence, with eight sacks on Deshaun Watson in their 17-12 success.

Love in the air as Packers dominate Bears

The 201st meeting of the NFL's oldest current rivalry went emphatically Green Bay's way with Jordan Love showing the importance of a franchise quarterback as the Packers pounded the Chicago Bears 31-7.

Love let it fly with 367 yards passing, including touchdowns of 42 and 53 yards to Christian Watson, while the Bears - without starter Caleb Williams - struggled with Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum under centre.

Williams stunned the Packers twice last season with fourth-quarter comebacks, including one in the play-offs, but Chicago are not the same threat without him.

They need their top man back from his hamstring injury as soon as possible.

After a tough start, last week's win over the Buffalo Bills was a huge confidence boost for the New England Patriots, as they showed with a 45-17 hammering of the Las Vegas Raiders.

Drake Maye has his critics after last season's Super Bowl loss, but 374 yards, four touchdown passes and one rushing score against a Las Vegas defence allowing 21 points a game previously was a huge effort.

It was a similar story with the Detroit Lions, who also hung 45 points on the Arizona Cardinals thanks to a monster game from running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who had 207 yards and two touchdowns.

Joining that pair on 3-2 is Aaron Rodgers and his Pittsburgh Steelers after a 34-22 win over the Indianpolis Colts.

Rodgers threw three touchdown passes to make it 582 in his career and move above the great Peyton Manning into third on the all-time list. Only Tom Brady (737) and Drew Brees (608) have more.

With 166 regular-season wins, Rodgers sits fifth on that list but, more importantly, his team look in decent shape in his final season.

We are already at the stage when struggling teams may be looking at top spot in next year's NFL Draft.

Three teams are now 0-5, with the Los Angeles Chargers, Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins all losing again.

Jim Harbaugh's Chargers are the big disappointment of the season. They suffered another self-inflicted defeat as poor play-calling and execution cost them the lead at the Denver Broncos.

They are 0-5 for the first time in 23 years.

Not much was expected of the Dolphins this season and they are not delivering as promised as they were outclassed again by Joe Burrow's Cincinnati Bengals.

The Titans scored only three points as they were bullied by the previously winless Houston Texans - in a nice boost for them before heading to London on Sunday.

articles.title: NFL Week 5: Don’t count out Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye just yet
articles.summary: Plus, three undefeated and three winless teams remain after a week of bizarre endings and bounce-back performances.
articles.body: Week 5 of the NFL season featured the latest chapter of one of the game’s most storied rivalries and resurgent performances from Aaron Rodgers and Drake Maye. Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday. Aaron Rodgers is heating up After having looked like one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL to start the season, Pittsburgh Steelers starter Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game, this time in a 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts. The last time Rodgers threw at least three touchdown passes in three straight games was in 2021, during his fourth MVP season with the Green Bay Packers. Rodgers is up to 10 touchdowns and four interceptions this year, and the Steelers improved to 3-2 with the win. The Packers earn a measure of revenge The Packers restored some balance in their rivalry with the Chicago Bears, defeating a Caleb Williams-less Bears squad 31-7. It was the teams’ first matchup since Chicago’s epic comeback in the wild-card round of last year’s playoffs. The Bears had won two in a row in the series, also authoring a come-from-behind win last regular season. This time, the Packers dominated on both sides of the ball. Green Bay held Ben Johnson’s offense in check, while Jordan Love had his finest game of the season. Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards, two touchdowns and a season-best 137.5 passer rating. Johnson has made no secret of his distaste for Green Bay since he took over in Chicago. After a frosty handshake following last winter’s playoff game, Johnson and Packers coach Matt LaFleur had a (relatively) friendly exchange Sunday. Drake Maye is fully back After a terrible start to the season, Maye, the New England Patriots quarterback, has now strung together two straight games reminiscent of the player who finished second in MVP voting in 2025. Maye threw for 374 yards and four touchdowns against the Las Vegas Raiders, also adding a score on the ground in a 45-17 win. In his last two games, he has thrown seven touchdown passes and only one interception. The Raiders were getting beaten so badly that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 overall pick in April’s NFL draft, got his first game action. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 48 yards. The Vikings stay undefeated The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 after they beat the New Orleans Saints 23-13. The Vikings continue to ride their defense, as their offense has been inconsistent at best this season. Quarterback Kyler Murray showed some improvement, however, completing 80% of his passes and posting a season-best 109.6 passer rating in the victory. Minnesota will play the Colts in Week 6 before its schedule gets tough: The Vikings will play the Detroit Lions, the Buffalo Bills, the Packers and the San Francisco 49ers in November. The Lions’ window to contend is still open Two years after the NFC North was the NFL’s best division, it’s full of good but not great teams. Count the Detroit Lions among them. The Lions’ 164 points (a 32.8-point average) are the second most in franchise history through five weeks of a season, but they have needed to score that much to outplay a porous defense allowing 29.6 points. On Sunday, after punts on their first three drives, the Lions (3-2) scored on their following seven consecutive possessions to easily beat Arizona and earn their first road win this season. A week of down-to-the-wire endings Sunday began with a stunner and ended with the season’s fifth overtime. In London, after Philadelphia took a lead with 8 seconds left, Jacksonville returned its ensuing kickoff deep enough to get into field-goal range and also fast enough to leave 1 second on the clock. The Jaguars then kicked a walk-off winning field goal to beat Philadelphia in what Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence called “maybe the craziest game I’ve ever been a part of.” Why kick it directly to a returner? “I lost us that game,” Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said. Even more inexplicable was Washington’s tie with the New York Giants, when the clock ran out in overtime before the Commanders, who didn’t have a timeout, could stop the clock and kick a field goal. Why allow quarterback Jayden Daniels to run the ball and keep the clock moving with only seconds left? Washington coach Dan Quinn blamed himself. “Sunday Night Football” on NBC offered an appropriate bookend to a wild day. After Baltimore scored a game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion with 40 seconds left in regulation, Atlanta couldn’t muster a game-winning drive when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. was hit hard and knocked out of the game. In the season’s fifth overtime game, Baltimore scored first and Atlanta had one final opportunity to match. But backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa threw an interception on Atlanta’s second play, and the Ravens (4-1) hung on 30-23. And then there were ... ... three undefeated teams and three winless teams left. San Francisco survived by inches to win in Seattle in one of the best games of the season to start 5-0 for the fifth time in the Super Bowl era. On the other end of the standings, Houston (1-4) and Tampa Bay (1-4) both earned their first wins during Week 5. Still searching for their own are Miami, Tennessee and the Los Angeles Chargers, all 0-5. The Chargers put together yet another performance full of either botched plays or bad luck, depending on your perspective, including a fumble by quarterback Justin Herbert when his own lineman’s foot accidentally kicked the ball out of his hand midway through the fourth quarter. The Chargers never led again after that turnover.

In October 2025, the tight end teamed up with JANA Partners to invest $200 million into Six Flags and just a year later, the amusement park is set to sell its parks.Travis Kelce’s Six Flags set to sell some locations in a $331 million deal amid constant lawsuitsAs per ABC News, Travis Kelce’s Six Flags is all set to sell 7 of its amusement parks across North America and one in Canada in a move that was "designed to sharpen operational focus while further enhancing its liquidity position."The seven affected parks of the Six Flags include Valleyfair in Minneapolis, Minnesota; Worlds of Fun in Kansas City, Missouri; Michigan's Adventure in Grand Rapids, Michigan; Schlitterbahn Waterpark Galveston in Galveston, Texas; Six Flags St. Louis in Eureka, Missouri; Six Flags Great Escape in Queensbury, New York; and Six Flags La Ronde, in Montreal, Quebec.As per reports, the agreement between Six Flags and EPR Properties includes a cash consideration of $331 million and is "subject to customary purchase price adjustments”.In a statement to ABC News, a Six Flags spokesperson said, "We understand how meaningful these parks are to the communities they serve and to the guests who have grown up visiting them. Our teams at these locations have created countless memories, and they are an important part of the Six Flags family.”The Six Flags spokesperson added, “We're confident in the future of these parks under the care of EPR and its operating partners, who have strong experience managing parks of this scale." They continued, "At the same time, this decision allows Six Flags to invest more deeply in the parks with the greatest opportunity for growth and innovation. We'll be better positioned to invest in new rides and attractions, upgrade park infrastructure and technology, enhance the guest experience with more immersive entertainment and introduce innovations that make every visit even more memorable."EPR Properties chair and CEO Gregory K. Silvers also weighed in on the deal with Six Flags as he said, "These properties embody the essential characteristics we seek: delivering stable, long-term cash flows, strong drive-to accessibility, multi-generational appeal, and significant underlying land value…”EPR Properties chair and CEO Gregory K. Silvers added, “This transaction aligns with our disciplined investment criteria and accelerates our strategic expansion into experiential properties that create enduring value for our shareholders."Travis Kelce remains distant as Six Flags remain busy with lawsuitsSix Flags’ move to sell 7 of its parks came at a time when the amusement park had to shut down its infamous rollercoaster X2 after settling a wrongful death lawsuit and currently fighting against 100 lawsuits filed by customers impacted by the rollercoaster.Despite the legal drama, Travis Kelce has kept himself away from the mess.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Roman Wilson Injured, Latest Rumors on Steelers WR's Timeline to Return from Finger Injury
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson is likely to miss multiple weeks due to a finger injury from Sunday's 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson is likely to miss multiple weeks due to a finger injury from Sunday's 34-22 win over the Indianapolis Colts, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Fowler reported he's seeking a second opinion.

Wilson was on the field for just 20 offensive snaps and got targeted once in the victory.

The third-year pass-catcher has already surpassed his production from 2025. He has 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns. His yards per game have almost tripled, going from 12.8 to 37.6.

This is another stroke of bad luck for Wilson. He was limited to one game as a rookie because of ankle and hamstring injuries. Toward the end of last year, he became a healthy scratch .

Wilson seemed to benefit from the offseason coaching change, but now his momentum will come to a halt.

The Steelers can ill afford to lose another receiver, either. Ben Skowronek (calf) also exited Sunday's game, and Michael Pittman Jr. is assured of missing at least the next three weeks after going on injured reserve.

Second-round pick Germie Bernard will need to step up in a big way to help ease the pressure on D.K. Metcalf.

articles.title: Justin Herbert’s fiancee Madison Beer bears the brunt of Chargers’ winless start while Emmanuel Acho calls FBI to get Los Angeles QB investigated
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh “doesn’t know” how to overturn a 0-5 record. He doesn’t know how to go about that embarrassing record.
articles.body: Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh “doesn’t know” how to overturn a 0-5 record. He doesn’t know how to go about that embarrassing record. If the coach is so hopeless about the team’s future, what can we expect from their quarterback, Justin Herbert?But luckily for the quarterback, he isn’t the one at the center of the criticism dartboard; it’s his fiancée, Madison Beer. Though he’s sitting just behind that dartboard, taking in all the throws. The pop star, however, has expectedly become the subject of Chargers fans’ crossfire.Justin Herbert’s fiancee Madison Beer becomes target of frustrated Chargers’ fans mockeryAfter the team lost to the Denver Broncos on Oct. 11 with a 23-17 score, frustrated fans began using the pop singer Madison Beer as bait for playful but harsh shots at the quarterback Justin Herbert.This unwanted attention was amplified previously when a Seahawks fan heckled Herbert during the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to Seattle. As Herbert entered the gridiron, the fan told him, “Hey Herbert! Herbert! Two meatball subs, you’re just as bad as your girl. You’re just as bad as your girl!”To top it off, Barstool Sports recently reposted Madison Beer News’ post from training camp - where the fiancée was comfortably sitting with her NFL better half on the practice ground, blissfully playing with his hair. Barstool Sports captioned their clip: “The Chargers still have not won a game since this video.”What can the Chargers do to redo their 2026 season recordThese are pure speculations! Read with caution. The Los Angeles Chargers could fire former Miami Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel - wherever he goes, losses follow. Remember Tua Tagovailoa? The Chargers could add more wide receivers because Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey are clearly not enough.They could bring in another quarterback, someone who is hardworking and not called a bust -like Mac Jones, Mason Rudolph, Jimmy Garoppolo, Jake Browning, Bailey Zappe, Jeff Driskel, Brandon Allen, Josh Johnson, Malik Willis, Tua Tagovailoa, Aidan O’Connell, Nick Mullens. Some of these names are popular, but whoever gets more gridiron time may actually want to prove something to everyone.Unlike Justin Herbert, who “seems” to be distracted by so many things, for instance, the love of his life - Madison Beer.They could fire first-year defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary because he hasn’t been able to use Khalil Mack. He recorded just 1 combined tackle vs. Denver Broncos!Mack recorded 32 combined tackles in 2025 and 20 in 2024. We’re already nearly halfway to the 2026 season! When will Mack come out of his shell? Or something’s up with Chris O’Leary…Amid countless number of suggestions for the Los Angeles Chargers, Justin Herbert reportedly becomes a target for an FBI investigation!SpeakEasy host Emmanuel Acho calls up FBI to investigate Justin HerbertSpeakEasy podcast host and former NFL player Emmanuel Acho probably crossed all limits of sanity and democracy when he dialed up the FBI to investigate Justin Herbert for a throw.Acho dialed “18**-2**-53**” on his podcast and said, “That’s the number for the FBI. Justin Herbert needs to be investigated because what is this?” pointing at a throw by Herbert that gave a direct pass to one of the Denver Broncos’ players, and not to the Los Angeles Chargers’ player just behind the Broncos player.“He’s throwing games! articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has built a public profile that extends well beyond her connection to Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. From fashion campaigns to beauty products and fitness partnerships, she has attracted brands looking to reach audiences interested in sport, wellness and lifestyle. Her growing commercial presence reflects how athletes’ families and public figures can develop their own identities in the marketing world. With partnerships involving established names such as Adidas and Abercrombie & Fitch, Brittany has expanded her reach across several industries while continuing to pursue opportunities connected to her passion for fitness and sports.Brittany Mahomes expands her brand endorsements across major industriesFashion and beauty have become important parts of Brittany Mahomes’ endorsement portfolio. Her partnership with Abercrombie & Fitch began in November 2025, giving the clothing retailer an opportunity to connect with consumers through her public profile and personal style.Adidas is another major name associated with her commercial activities. The relationship places her in the beauty and personal care market, where social media visibility can help brands introduce products to new audiences.Alani Nu has also featured in her endorsement portfolio. The energy drink brand has worked with Brittany on promotions involving flavours such as Hawaiian Shaved Ice, connecting her fitness-focused image with a product aimed at active consumers.Her association with Vitality, formerly known as Balance Athletica, adds an apparel dimension. As a co-owner, she has a stake in a business connected to the growing visibility of women’s football in the United States.She has also appeared in campaigns for CommunityAmerica Credit Union alongside Patrick Mahomes, bringing their family profile into financial services marketing. Her appearance in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue further broadened her visibility beyond sports and fitness audiences.Another partnership connects Brittany with WHOOP, a wearable technology company focused on health and fitness tracking. The association fits naturally with her athletic interests and the wider demand for products that help consumers monitor their daily activity.Taken together, these partnerships show the range of opportunities available to Brittany Mahomes.
