articles.title: Report Card Grades for Browns' NFL Week 5 Game vs. Jets
articles.summary: Dreary. Grim. Disappointing.
articles.body:
Those words described more than the weather on a rainy afternoon at MetLife Stadium. They also captured the Cleveland Browns' offensive performance in a 17-12 loss to the New York Jets in Week 5.

The Browns squandered an opportunity to start the season 4-1 in a game defined by poor pass protection, missed opportunities and a miserable ground game. Their defense did enough to give them a chance to win, but the offense couldn't capitalize.

Let's take a look at Sunday's performance through the lens of grades for the key players.

The only reason this grade isn't lower is that this was the worst performance from the offensive line all season. Watson had pressure in his face often and their inability to create a clean pocket played into Watson's performance.

That being said, there was plenty of ugly from the quarterback too.

The weather played a role. The conditions weren't ideal for a big game statistically, but he completed just 15 of his 33 pass attempts for 155 yards. There were drops in there, but there were plenty of throws that he missed as well.

To Watson's credit, he didn't have an interception. Unfortunately, he also had three fumbles. Only one was recovered by the Jets. Escaping the game with just one turnover was one of the few positives.

Judkins (14 carries, 44 yards) once again struggled to find much daylight in the run game. How much of that is on him is debatable. Regardless, it's hard to give him much credit when the run game completely failed just as it needed to step up in the rain.

Sanders had very little to offer outside of a five-yard run in relief of Judkins. He's shown some juice in the passing game, but his only catch this week went for a yard.

The rookie receiver was knocked out of the game with a concussion after a head-to-head collision with Minkah Fitzpatrick. The passing game dysfunction in his absence is a credit to what he does for them as a quick-game/screen threat.

Boston gets credit for coming down with the only touchdown of the game for the Browns offense, but it's worth noting that he was bailed out earlier on the drive. He dropped a pass, but Brandon Stephens was flagged for questionable pass interference on the play.

The Browns needed more than the three catches and 46 yards he gave them today.

Remember when Jerry Jeudy showed up last week, quit being invisible and actually had a positive impact on the game? Well, his Week 5 performance was one to forget. Three catches for 19 yards on seven targets was another inefficient game for him.

With Concepcion out, the Browns were forced to get Bond involved in the offense. He led the team with 74 yards on three receptions. Good. He also had multiple crucial drops and probably could have turned his 30-yard catch into a much bigger gain if he just stayed in bounds and kept running. Bad.

NFL Season Shaping Up To Be Unpredictable 🗣️

It's hard to pin all of this grade on Fannin himself. He's somewhat dependent on schemed touches and Watson just didn't look his way early in the game. However, he only came down with one of his four targets so he was a complete non-factor.

That's not acceptable on an afternoon where Concepcion was forced out of the lineup.

Fano was beaten by a bull rush from David Bailey for a sack. Most of Bailey's success came on the right side, but Fano should be charged with at least one sack.

Ironically enough, this may have been Zion Johnson's best game in a Browns uniform. He was not the problem in pass protection and he played a relatively clean game.

Jenkins wasn't terrible in pass pro himself, but there were a few breakdowns in blitz pickup where the communication was off. The lack of any interior push in the run game was partially on him as well.

This one goes down as Barber's weakest game thus far. He struggled handling Jowon Briggs' power and he wasn't great in the run game either.

It was yet another rough one for Tytus Howard as the right tackle. He was in and out of the game with a knee injury which may explain some of his struggles.

He managed to avoid more false starts, but he was a big reason that David Bailey looked like Myles Garrett.

Dawand Jones came in for 33 snaps while Howard dealt with his knee injury. He wasn't an upgrade and couldn't handle Bailey's speed coming off the edge.

Box score watchers won't be impressed with Verse this week. He registered just three tackles and no sacks. However, he was collapsing the pocket and flushing Geno Smith right to the interior defensive linemen on multiple occasions.

McGuire got involved with Adin Huntington and Maliek Collins on a sack. He was another one whose work didn't necessarily show up in the box score, but he was effective in the Browns stunts up front that caused a lot of chaos for Geno Smith and the Jets offensive line.

Williams didn't get a ton of opportunities to rush the passer in this one. Most of the edge pressure came from Verse and McGuire, but Williams didn't look bad when he was on the field.

No Mason Graham. No Mike Hall Jr. No problem. Maliek Collins had to cause disruption on the interior with two of the Browns best interior defenders out for the game.

He rose to the occasion with 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits. The Jets interior offensive line had a hard time dealing with Collins quick first step throughout the afternoon.

Huntington was another one who stepped up in the pass-rush department. He was able to knife in for half a sack, but he also had six total tackles and a quarterback hit.

He might not have always kept the best run fit, but he made big plays.

Kamara got the practice squad call up with injuries piling up on the outside. He joined in on the fun with a quarterback sack, but it was an uneven performance for the interior as a whole with Braelon Allen rushing for 116 yards on 24 carries.

The linebacker duo of Schwesinger and Williams were among the brightest spots on an otherwise dreary Sunday. Schwesinger was all over the field and made impact plays with a forced fumble and tackle for loss.

There's always an expectation that a player will bring a little extra juice when playing their former team. Williams lived up to that and more. Creating three forced fumbles and a tackle for loss highlighted an awesome performance.

This wasn't Ward's best game. The Jets moved Garrett Wilson around so Ward wasn't always covering their best receiver, however, he was at fault for some of Wilson's seven catches for 104 yards.

It isn't often that Campbell grades out higher than Ward, but he was the best corner on Sunday. He made few notable blunders in coverage, but it's worth noting that he took out two Browns defenders on Braelon Allen's go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter.

Harden wasn't picked on in this one and mostly held his own in coverage. It was interesting that the Brown gave Mekhi Blackmon a few snaps in the slot. Harden might have some competition moving forward.

Delpit might not have played the best coverage all day. He gave up four receptions on six targets, per PFF . However, he jammed Wilson at the line in some of the Browns zone coverages and was a factor in the run game as well.

Hickman missed a crucial tackle on Garrett Wilson on the opening drive touchdown. It wasn't the only one that he missed. Hickman was fine in coverage, but the run of missed tackles in one-on-one situations is becoming a recurring issue.

The rookie continues to play well in his third safety role. He had an interception that was negated by a Maliek Collins offsides penalty. Perhaps more importantly, he played 29 defensive snaps with no major issues.

Szmyt missed his first kick of the season when he pushed a PAT to the right. Still, he went 2-for-2 on his field goals with a long of 41.

Corey Bojorquez had a busy day at the office. The Browns had to call on him to punt eight times and he averaged 52.6 yards per boot.

Unfortunately, that's all overshadowed by the high snap that went through his hands with just under four minutes to go and set up the Jets with a short field to score the go-ahead touchdown.

articles.title: Mike Evans’ brutal dig at Stefon Diggs’ brother Trevon Diggs reportedly promoted by former Seahawks star Richard Sherman
articles.summary: Mike Evans joined the NFL in 2014. A year later, Stefon Diggs entered the league.
articles.body: Mike Evans joined the NFL in 2014. A year later, Stefon Diggs entered the league. Then in 2020, Diggs’ younger brother Trevon Diggs was drafted by the Dallas Cowboys.It’s not unlikely for a player who is a 12-year veteran to not know someone who’s a 5-year veteran. It just speaks to obliviousness. How inattentive, heedless, and unaware Mike Evans must be to ignore what is happening around him.Yes, he’s more into his game. But to insult someone who has been in the league for almost six years?That speaks to immaturity and rowdiness, as if he could do anything on the gridiron just because he’s winning all the games after he transferred from a losing team [Tampa Bay Buccaneers] to a Super Bowl-contending team [San Francisco 49ers].Mike Evans checks Stefon Diggs’ brother Trevon Diggs’ jerseyMike Evans delivered one of the most memorable trash-talking moments of the 2026 NFL season. Cyberspace won’t let it disappear anytime soon. Not now, not ever.The San Francisco 49ers wide receiver got into a heated exchange with Seattle Seahawks cornerback Trevon Diggs during their Week 5 clash on October 11 at Lumen Field in Seattle.The one-minute confrontation stood out as the most embarrassing moment because of Mike Evans’ dismissive response. Instead of just exchanging words with the Seahawks cornerback, the veteran wide receiver turned Diggs around to check the name on the back of his jersey.Evans grabbed Diggs by the shoulders and turned him around to look at his nameplate, as if questioning the identity of the player confronting him. Or maybe he was disrespecting him while the cameras were watching? Anyhow, it became a viral moment that had NFL fans laughing because they weren’t ready for it!Mike Evans could not recognize Trevon DiggsMike Evans later justified his disrespectful actions. Speaking after the San Francisco 49ers’ 32-29 victory over the Seattle Seahawks, the veteran said that he had been blocking Diggs until the whistle and believed the cornerback accused him of doing extra.The veteran added that he initially didn’t recognize Diggs because helmets can make identification difficult.“I didn’t know that was him at first, because I played against him a few times, and we’ve always been cool. He was a good player. And I honestly didn’t know it was him because in the helmet, it’s hard to tell sometimes,” Evans explained.After Evans checked Diggs’ back, Diggs probably felt disrespected, so he pushed Evans back by knocking on his helmet.Richard Sherman found the Mike Evans Trevon Diggs moment funnyFormer Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers cornerback and current NFL analyst Richard Sherman truly enjoyed the Mike Evans-Trevon Diggs exchange. He called it a perfect example of on-field trash talk.“Mike Evans checking to see the name on the back of the jersey is an all-time GIF and trash-talk moment that I wish I would have thought of.” If analysts approve of this as something funny, what will future veterans do to junior veterans? articles.summary: Parker Washington's one-handed catch and a game-winning 57-yard field goal headlined NFL Week 5's most clutch plays and touchdown highlights.
articles.body: Week 5 of the NFL season was especially fun to watch. Several games came down to the wire, a few miscues led to losses and even ties and there were clutch moments that made Sunday exciting. At least five touchdown catches during the slate of games were worth highlighting. The Jacksonville Jaguars’ Parker Washington, Minnesota Vikings’ Justin Jefferson, Green Bay Packers’ Christian Watson, Cincinnati Bengals’ Ja’Marr Chase and Arizona Cardinals’ Trey McBride each made scoring grabs that may make the highlight reel once Week 18 is all over. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Let’s take a look at some of those plays that left you hooting and hollering from the couch. Washington’s London grab The Jaguars needed to make a play late in their game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Time was of the essence as Philadelphia owned a 14-10 lead late in the game. With 3:20 left, Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington going up the sideline. Lawrence threw a pass on 4th-and-5 only Washington would be able to catch. The wide receiver leaped from the 2-yard line, made a one-handed grab around an Eagles defender and landed in the end zone. Jacksonville took a 16-14 lead at that point. The Eagles were able to march down the field and take the lead back thanks to a Jake Elliott 48-yard field goalwith 8 seconds left in the game. But a special teams miscue allowed the Jaguars to move the ball up the field and set Cam Little up for the game-winning 57-yard field goal. Washington finished with six catches for 124 yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson in rhythm Justin Jefferson’s touchdown might not have been as clutch as Washington’s but it was just as pretty. The Vikings trailed the New Orleans Saints 7-6 in the third quarter and had the ball in the red zone. Kyler Murray batted the ball and found Jefferson in the end zone. A Saints defender misjudged the ball and it landed in the hands of Jefferson. Somehow, Jefferson was able to fall backward and still make the catch with three New Orleans players around him. The touchdown gave the Vikings the lead at that point. Minnesota held on for the 23-13 victory. Jefferson finished with six catches for 79 yards and a touchdown. Dear, Watson If you just looked at the scoreboard and thought the Packers completely owned the Chicago Bears, you would have never guessed Green Bay only led by a touchdown coming out of halftime. That all changed thanks to the connection between Jordan Love and Christian Watson. On 3rd-and-22, Love dropped back to pass and launched the football 53 yards and found Watson in the back of the end zone. Watson made the catch on top of the Bears defender’s head and stayed in bounds. Green Bay took a 21-7 lead and didn’t look back. The Packers won 31-7. Watson finished with six catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Eye of the Bengal The Bengals probably got a little more from the Miami Dolphins than they originally bargained for. The Dolphins clawed their way back in the fourth quarter but couldn’t do enough to force overtime. Cincinnati won the game 31-24. As the Bengals were rolling in the middle of the game, Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase hooked up for a big touchdown. Burrow found Chase in the end zone late in the third quarter. The catch was far from routine. Chase had a Dolphins defensive back on him. He was able to box him out around the 1-yard line and twist his way into the end zone for the magnificent touchdown. The 45-yard touchdown proved to be crucial in the Bengals’ win. Chase had six catches for 77 yards and the score. Tip drill Each of the four catches mentioned previously came in wins. The touchdown grabs played a significant part in those teams’ victories on Sunday. Generally, the good teams will find a way to win no matter the obstacle they have to overcome to get it. It was a little different in Arizona. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals were in garbage time against the Detroit Lions, trying to salvage some points as to not make the blowout look worse than it was. Brissett was in the red zone when he found Trey McBride with a smidge of opportunity to make a catch. The star tight end went over one defender, tipped the ball to himself and was able to get both feet down to make the catch. articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 6 Rankings, Projections and Waiver-Wire Tips
articles.summary: The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are effectively finished.
articles.body:
The first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season are effectively finished.

How have the fantasy football gods treated you so far?

Ideally, you're managing a juggernaut. Your start and sit decisions are the kind where there are no wrong answers. You're going into matchups wondering how wide your margin of victory will be this time around.

For most of you, though, that is not the case. Maybe it's nowhere close. Considering the damage done by the injury bug, and the bye-week absences, you might be struggling to just put a functional lineup together.

Either way, we're here to help with early Week 6 rankings and waiver-wire targets at the three marquee positions.

Waiver-wire target: Jordan Love, GB (vs. DAL)

Love's passing yardage has lacked consistency, but his good games have been pretty awesome. So far, he has either thrown for less than 200 yards (twice) or more than 300 (three times). This volatility is impossible to trust on a weekly basis, but his arrow should be pointing all the way up against a Cowboys defense allowing the second-most fantasy points to the position, per Yahoo Sports.

Projected stats: 26-of-34 passing for 287 yards, three touchdowns

Waiver-wire target: Marshawn Lloyd, GB (vs. DAL)

Things haven't quite fully quicked for Lloyd just yet, but he is getting the kind of opportunities that suggest it's only a matter of time. He's already tallied double-digit carries in two games, and he saw five targets in another. After taking some flak for not supporting his hometown Chicago Bears, longtime Green Bay Packers fan and NBA superstar Anthony Davis got the last laugh.

Prior to the rivalry game, Davis made a friendly jersey challenge to Dyon Brooks on Instagram . After the Packers defeated the Bears 31-7 on Sunday, Chicago wide receiver Luther Burden III commented on Davis' post. Davis then responded by trolling Burden, commenting, "Heard you ain't wanna play today champ!"

Davis was referring to Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin's fiery shots at Burden when he told reporters after the game, "He quit today. He didn't wanna play no more."

Burden made himself a target for the Packers and fans like Davis after he provided bulletin-board material ahead of the Week 5 matchup. When asked about Bears head coach Ben Johnson's message before facing their NFC North rivals, Burden told reporters , "He wants to beat them really bad like everyone else in the room, like every Chicago fan. Beat them real bad, and make them quit."

Instead, Green Bay made a statement with Sunday's victory, forcing five turnovers and shutting out Chicago for the entire second half to secure the win. Burden led the Bears with 47 receiving yards on four catches, but his team couldn't overcome its slew of mistakes. Chicago was also playing without star quarterback Caleb Williams for a third straight game while he recovers from a hamstring injury.

Sunday's performance was a cause for celebration for Packers fans like Davis, who had also proposed a challenge to comedian Dyon Brooks in which the losing fan has to wear the winning team's jersey.

At 3-2, Green Bay is now tied with Chicago and the Detroit Lions for the second-best record in the NFC North behind the first-place Minnesota Vikings, who are one of three remaining undefeated teams at 5-0.

Davis will be hoping to watch the Packers earn their third straight win when they meet the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) on Sunday Night Football in Week 6.

articles.title: Week 6 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Germie Bernard, Kendre Miller, Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: In certain weeks, the fantasy football waiver wire appears overloaded with intriguing options.
articles.body:
In certain weeks, the fantasy football waiver wire appears overloaded with intriguing options.

Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season does not appear to be one of those weeks.

The problem is this lack of excitement may not have any bearing on your need to work the waivers. With four teams on a bye in Week 6 (the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins and Minnesota Vikings) and the injury report perpetually piling up, some managers will find themselves needing multiple pickups.

It's not all doom and gloom, by the way. There are viable targets—we'll spotlight three who are rostered in fewer than 50 percent of fantasy leagues, per FantasyPros —and while they may not scream excitement, they should be capable streamers and could emerge as more if they surprise.

Germie Bernard, WR, Pittsburgh Steelers (6% Rostered)

Pittsburgh's passing attack is really perking up. In fact, that surge is directly responsible for two of our three recommendations here.

The first is Germie Bernard, a second-round rookie out of Alabama. He had kept pretty quiet through the first four weeks—though he did see eight targets in Week 2 (they yielded only four catches for 35 yards)—but Week 5 was a totally different story. His stat line showed one personal-best after the next, as he finished with six receptions on nine targets for 80 yards. He even handled his first career carry.

"We were focused on Germie getting more opportunities today," coach Mike McCarthy told reporters afterward. "He definitely delivered."

The Steelers have no reasons to rethink this strategy. That option may not be available anyway, since Michael Pittman Jr. is on injured reserve, and Roman Wilson could be out multiple weeks with a finger injury. If Bernard makes the most of this opportunity, he'll challenge the notion that there aren't exciting waiver targets available.

Kendre Miller, RB, New Orleans Saints (8% Rostered)

When the waiver wire is really cooking, it offers up players who have impressed with both volume and efficiency. So far, though, Kendre Miller is only covering one side of that coin.

This is a volume-only recommendation, but at least the volume is encouraging. In two of four games, Miller has handled at least nine carries. He scored in both of those contests, too.

His passing work is nearly nonexistent, though, and his efficiency leaves a lot to be desired. His average touch is spanning just 3.0 yards. He isn't averaging even three yards per carry or four yards per catch.

That volume keeps coming, though, and it feels unlikely to change, especially with Alvin Kamara being limited by a back injury. This is also the least efficient Miller has ever been with his touches (career 4.3 yards per touch), so some positive regression could help make a lot more out of these volume opportunities.

Aaron Rodgers, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers (27% Rostered)

Remember that aforementioned turnaround with Pittsburgh's passing attack? Well, it has turned Aaron Rodgers into a fantasy star again.

Question the sustainability all you want, but here's the truth: Only two quarterbacks have tallied more fantasy points since Week 3 than Rodgers. On Sunday, he threw three touchdown passes for the third consecutive week while shattering his previous season-high with 71 percent passing.

"This might be the best Rodgers has looked since joining the Steelers," Adam Bittner noted for USA Today . "At his current pace, he'd throw 34 touchdowns this season. That would be his most since 2021, and only his third 30-touchdown season since 2017."

For a long while, it felt like Rodgers' days of fantasy relevance were behind him. And maybe it'll look like that again soon. For those needing a jolt at quarterback, though, it's hard not to react to an all-time great engineering a run this hot. The fact it could end at any moment doesn't mean it's actually destined to end any time soon.

articles.title: “To give children the hope and the opportunity to learn”: How Tom Brady helped thousands of children access better learning opportunities with a 1,000-laptop donation

articles.body: Tom Brady has made several contributions away from the football field, including a donation that helped children gain access to technology and educational resources. In Feb. 2009, the former New England Patriots quarterback donated 1,000 laptops to One Laptop per Child with support from the New England Patriots Charitable Foundation. Brady also visited a Boston-area club to meet children and demonstrate how the computers worked.How Tom Brady’s 1,000-laptop donation aimed to expand learning opportunitiesBrady supported the One Laptop per Child campaign founded by Nicholas Negroponte. The initiative focused on giving children access to affordable computers, particularly in communities where educational technology was difficult to obtain.During his visit to the West End House Boys and Girls Club in Allston, Massachusetts, Brady brought XO laptops for children to explore. The computers featured a colour screen, internet connectivity and educational programmes designed to help children learn and communicate.Brady explained why the initiative meant so much to him.“I've been blessed with many opportunities to have traveled around the world, and I've been to Africa, been to some impoverished places around the world, and to give children the hope and the opportunity to learn and to expand their vision of the world is extremely important,” Brady said in February 2009.His personal connection to the project also extended to his family. Brady revealed that his sister had spent five months in Uganda, where children had recently received laptops for their classroom.“It's exciting for me to be here to show some support and create some awareness for what Nicholas has done. It's an incredible vision,” he added.The donation was intended to reach children beyond the United States, with the 1,000 computers distributed through One Laptop per Child's participating countries and Boys and Girls Clubs across New England. articles.summary: One NFL executive thought the Baltimore Ravens took an unprecedented step before receiving the necessary assurances to sign off on a trade for offensive lineman Cam Jurgens.
articles.body:
One NFL executive thought the Baltimore Ravens took an unprecedented step before receiving the necessary assurances to sign off on a trade for offensive lineman Cam Jurgens.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Saturday the Ravens staged a physical on Jurgens at the Philadelphia Eagles' facility.

NFL Season Shaping Up To Be Unpredictable 🗣️

"I have never heard of that being done," the exec told Mike Sando of The Athletic.

The fallout from the failed Maxx Crosby trade is lingering months after the fact.

In early March, the Ravens and Las Vegas Raiders agreed to terms on a blockbuster swap centered around the five-time Pro Bowler. Days later, the deal was off altogether. Baltimore reportedly had concerns about Crosby's left knee after he underwent a physical and backed out.

Sando wrote there was a sense around the league the saga "would make it tough for teams to take Baltimore at its word on a significant trade."

There was no such risk of that happening with the Jurgens deal since the Ravens went the extra mile.

"I think it's the only way you could ever deal with the Ravens again," the executive said to Sando.

The exec did, however, question whether the on-site physical is something Baltimore can duplicate in every trade moving forward.

"The fact that Baltimore and Philly are so close, they can drive that and it can happen," they said. "But let's say San Francisco makes the same deal. They're gonna fly all these medical people back there in two days to go through this?"

Speaking to The Athletic's Michael Silver in April, Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta said rival GMs were initiating trade discussions with him, supposedly illustrating how the Crosby ordeal wasn't adversely impacting his job.

The circumstances behind the acquisition of Jurgens seem to paint a different picture.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. Rumors Reveal How WR Orchestrated Trade to Texans amid Frustration with Cards
articles.summary: The "frustration had been mounting" with wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. prior to his exit from the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
The "frustration had been mounting" with wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. prior to his exit from the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Rapoport reported that Harrison, who had been without representation, hired agents to help facilitate a trade.

According to Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Cardinals are sending Harrison and a seventh-round pick to the Houston Texans for a 2027 second-round pick and a sixth-rounder.

The arc of Harrison's Arizona tenure is a shock to anybody who watched him in college at Ohio State. He looked like an NFL-ready wideout as a sophomore in 2022 and finished fourth in the 2023 Heisman Trophy voting.

As he entered the pros, the two-time All-American was seemingly the closest you can get to a sure thing in the draft.

Instead, Harrison had a solid rookie season before going backward in 2025. Things then hit a nadir in the Cardinals' first four games as he was targeted just 13 times (five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown).

Having Jacoby Brissett, a proven hand with a low ceiling, at quarterback only goes so far to explain Harrison's terrible production, too. Tight end Trey McBride has an NFL-high 42 receptions, and Michael Wilson (29 catches) ranks in the top 10.

Brissett is throwing the ball — his 199 attempts are second only to the New Orleans Saints' Tyler Shough. He just wasn't looking Harrison's way.

Harrison will now have a clean slate in Houston, and he gets to reunite with former Buckeyes teammate C.J. Stroud.

However, The Athletic's Mike Sando pointed out this is only the fifth time since 2002 a top-five NFL draft pick got traded before logging three full seasons. That puts him in the same company as Trey Lance, Trent Richardson and Aaron Curry, none of whom thrived after a change of scenery.

The onus is squarely on Harrison to prove he's better than what he put on tape with the Cardinals.

articles.summary: The Eagles' running back is being heavily tested early in the 2026 season.
articles.body:
When the Philadelphia Eagles head into Week 6, they'll likely do so with their fourth-string running back as their starter. Third-string running back Will Shipley reportedly sustained a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday's game and is expected to miss weeks due to the injury, according to ESPN.

Shipley sustained the injury early in the team's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Shipley finished the contest with five carries for six yards and a touchdown. With Shipley out of the game, Dameon Pierce received every single running back carry. He finished with 11 attempts for 14 yards.

The injury leaves the Eagles exceptionally thin at running back. Starter Saquon Barkley missed Week 5 due to an injured hamstring and backup Tank Bigsby was placed on injured reserve ahead of the contest due to a core muscle issue. Coming into the game, the team had to promote Pierce and Carson Steele from the practice squad for depth reasons. Steele did not record a touch in Week 5.

With Shipley sidelined, Pierce could see an even bigger role moving forward if Barkley is unable to return. Steele could also get run as the team's backup and Jaydon Blue could be the next running back called up from the team's practice squad.

Coming off a last-second loss to the Jaguars in London, the Eagles' task won't get much easier in Week 6. The team will take on the upstart Carolina Panthers, which are averaging 30.3 points per game.

articles.title: Mike Evans has given Kyle Shanahan and San Francisco 49ers their Julio Jones, says Neil Reynolds
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Jeff Reinebold discuss a dramatic Week Five in the 2026 NFL season, including the San Francisco 49ers' thrilling win over the Seattle Seahawks; listen to Neil, Jeff and Phoebe Schecter on the Inside the Huddle podcast through the campaign
articles.body:
If there was any doubt as to whether Mike Evans could still dominate at the highest level in the NFL, he has quickly shut down such narratives in his first month with the San Francisco 49ers.

The veteran wide receiver starred on Sunday as he made seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown in his side's 32-29 win over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks.

Evans signed a three-year $42.4m deal with the 49ers this offseason following 12 years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with whom he recorded 11 straight 1,000-yard campaigns.

"Kyle Shanahan hasn't had that since he was offensive coordinator in Atlanta with Julio Jones," said Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds.

"Hostile environment. 50-50 balls, going up and making amazing catches. Also, just as we were talking about Mike Evans making amazing catch after amazing catch, I dropped my pen, so not all of us can make amazing catches."

The win lifted Kyle Shanahan's side to a perfect 5-0 on the year at the top of the NFC West, while also marking Evans' first 100-yard game for the 49ers.

"I don't know if Kyle Shanahan gets enough credit," said Sky Sports' Jeff Reinebold. "Everybody talks about all the superstars he's got. We talk about great coaches always go to players, not plays.

"I want to spread the joy in if you're a Niner fan. What did you bring Mike Evans to San Francisco for? Performances like that.

"They have not had that kind of guy in that offense. That big, physical, contested catch, red zone target guy that you can't win it, whether it's a first down or a touchdown in the red zone, you know he's gonna be the guy if you just give him a chance.

"And I thought Brock Purdy gave him a chance and that's what you get."
